attribution.note: Zitron speaks these words himself as interviewer, in his own published interview. They are not Acemoglu's.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both parts of the statement. The contract scores only the slowing-growth part and treats the 'no new thing to acquire' part as context. That split is reasonable because the second part has no test.

contract.note: No company list, metric or baseline was given. Reading 'growth is slowing' as latest-quarter revenue growth against a year earlier is ordinary. Q1 2023 was a weak base, and a multi-year baseline could give a different result, but the reading is not stretched. The choice of companies and baseline determines the result.

evidence.note: Microsoft's revenue grew 17% in the quarter ended March 2024. Microsoft's own release.
Microsoft's year-earlier baseline was 7%. Read with e1, growth sped up.
Meta's revenue grew 27% in Q1 2024. Verbatim reprint of the release.
Meta's Q1 2023 baseline was 3%. Read with e3, growth sped up sharply.
Apple's revenue fell 4% in the March 2024 quarter. The support condition counts a decline.

reviews.rationale: Of five firms, Microsoft and Meta sped up (contradict) and Apple declined (supports). Alphabet's and Amazon's releases could not be read, so neither side reaches the 'most' threshold the contract requires. The packet does not settle the outcome.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words as interviewer in his published interview.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the GPT-4o target, the 18-month window and 'not significantly different'.

contract.note: Using GPT-4 (March 2023) as the baseline fits the 18-month window. 'Not significantly different' is broad, so counting major new modalities alongside core capability is a fair, ordinary reading. 'Significantly' has no threshold, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: OpenAI says GPT-4o matches GPT-4 Turbo on text, reasoning and coding. This is a company disclosure, and Turbo itself came out within the window.
OpenAI calls it a 'GPT-4 level model' and frames the gain as efficiency and access. Company disclosure.
A single end-to-end model with native audio and vision. Voice latency falls from 5.4 s to about 320 ms. Company disclosure.
On LMSYS Arena-Hard, GPT-4o has a 79% judged win rate against GPT-4-0314 (baseline 50), and MMLU is somewhat higher. The judge is a GPT-4-class model. Dated before the post.

reviews.rationale: Against the March 2023 GPT-4 baseline, GPT-4o was clearly preferred on hard prompts and added native audio and vision with much lower latency. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. Its text parity with GPT-4 Turbo backs only a narrower claim than 'not significantly different' over 18 months.
